name: Documentary 3D
description: Dark cinematic 3D data documentary for history, economy, science, technology and geography stories. ONE persistent stage laid out as a gallery of set pieces along a path (a lit globe with a glowing route, blueprint sheets on a wood desk, a domed building at dusk, a locomotive driving toward the camera, a particle map with a flowing route, a ledger with a red underline, a night aircraft, a wheat field at sunset, an empty bowl on cracked earth); the camera flies from one set piece to the next, each scene one metaphor with real beats (trains moving, particles flowing, counters ticking, light rising). Dusk lighting with a warm low key and a cool rim, haze, volumetric light shafts, bloom, a dissolve between scenes, big animated number pills (`counter` overlay) and word-synced captions in the upper middle. Parametric builders for the set pieces: globe, train, rail-track, dome-building, aircraft, ledger, blueprint-sheet, desk-wood, wheat-field, bowl, cracked-ground, particle-map. No emoji.
prompt_hint: 10-18 scenes (2.5-4 s) about ONE story told with numbers (any topic: a historical project, an economy, a scientific discovery, a technology, a place). Build the world ONCE in a top-level `stage` (gallery: every set piece is an actor at its own spot along a path, 8-10 units apart; add a dark `world.ground` plane and plinths) from `{ "build": "<name>", "params": {...}, "seed": n }` calls (run `node cli.mjs builders`). One scene = one metaphor: the camera flies to the next set piece with `shots` (`focus` + `frame`; a hard `cut: true` only for a deliberate jump), the set piece does something real with `beats` (a train drives toward the camera, particles flow along a route, light rises, a hammer drives a spike) and a `counter` overlay counts the key number. Use `spotlight` fx for light shafts and `signal` fx for particles on a path. Narration in short sentences; captions are word by word in the upper middle. No emoji.
best_for: history told with numbers (a railway, a canal, a war, a discovery)
economy and finance stories (trade, prices, debt, harvests)
geography and logistics: routes, flows, distances

gallery-flight.subject: A story with 8-10 set pieces along a path, for example how a country was connected by a railway.
gallery-flight.when: Each scene needs its own recognizable metaphor but the video must feel like one continuous camera shot.
gallery-flight.beats: wide on the first set piece -> light rises on it (a spotlight fx, an emissive beat) -> its real action (a beat) -> the camera flies on to the next set piece while the narration continues -> repeat -> pull out over the whole gallery.
gallery-flight.shots: wide -> zoom-to each set piece in order (frame medium or close, a low or orbit yaw) -> wide at the end; `cut: true` only for a jump on purpose.
gallery-flight.builders: globe, blueprint-sheet, desk-wood, dome-building, train, rail-track, particle-map, ledger, aircraft, wheat-field, bowl, cracked-ground, ship, mountain, sun

number-story.subject: One quantity that grows, for example people, days, kilometres or money.
number-story.when: The point of the video is a number that changes over the scenes.
number-story.beats: a set piece that stands for the quantity (a particle map, a ledger, a chart) -> the `counter` overlay counts to the first value -> steps raise it scene after scene -> the set piece reacts (more particles, a taller stack) -> the last counter is the punchline.
number-story.shots: zoom-to the set piece, slow push-in with each step.

journey.subject: Something that travels, for example a train, a ship or an aircraft across the map.
journey.when: A route is the story: A to B, with places in between.
journey.beats: the vehicle starts far away on the path -> beat pos moves it toward the camera -> trail fx behind it -> the globe or map route lights up segment by segment (`route-k` beats) -> arrival and a counter with the duration.
journey.shots: low hero angle on the vehicle, orbit, fly-through, pull-back to the map.
journey.builders: train, rail-track, ship, aircraft, globe, particle-map, mountain
